title: Nemytskii operators on Lebesgue spaces
abstract: Develops superposition operators induced by Caratheodory functions: measurability, Lp-to-Lq growth bounds and sequential continuity, Lipschitz estimates, monotonicity and coercivity, and Frechet remainder estimates. For Lebesgue measure on the real line and finite-dimensional real fibers, characterizes when every Lp input has an Lq output by the standard integrable-envelope growth condition, for 1 <= p,q < infinity. First-order remainder estimates on arbitrary measure spaces assume a Caratheodory derivative with the stated Holder-compatible growth. The integral-functional result bounds the integrated remainder and proves integrability of the linearized integrand; it does not assert integrability of the original integrand without its separate growth hypotheses. Caratheodory here requires strongly measurable sections and almost-everywhere continuity in the fiber variable.

informal.NemytskiiLebesgue.IsCaratheodory.memLp_n: For f from R times R^m to R^k with strongly measurable sections and almost-everywhere continuous fibers, and 1 <= p,q < infinity, every Lp input gives an Lq output if and only if there exist an Lq real envelope a and a nonnegative constant C such that almost everywhere, simultaneously for every fiber vector xi, norm(f(x,xi)) <= abs(a(x)) + C * norm(xi)^(p/q).
informal.NemytskiiLebesgue.IsCaratheodory.nemytsk: On any measure space, the same Caratheodory and growth assumptions imply that a sequence of Lp functions converging in Lp to an Lp function has superposition images converging in Lq, for finite exponents p,q at least one and finite-dimensional real fibers.
informal.NemytskiiLebesgue.IsCaratheodory.eLpNorm: On a measure space, suppose f and its fiber derivative f' are Caratheodory, f' is the Frechet derivative at every fiber point almost everywhere, p,r >= 1 satisfy 1/q = 1/r + 1/p, and f' is bounded by b + C * norm(xi)^(p/r) with nonnegative b in Lr and C > 0. At each Lp function u, the Lq integral quantity (a quasi-norm when q < 1) of the first-order remainder is at most epsilon times the Lp norm of l whenever l is in Lp and its Lp norm is sufficiently small.
informal.NemytskiiLebesgue.IsCaratheodory.integra: On a measure space with finite-dimensional real inputs, under Caratheodory assumptions on f and its fiber derivative f', conjugate exponents p,q, and derivative growth b + C*norm(xi)^(p-1) with nonnegative b in Lq and C > 0, the linearized integrand is integrable for every Lp perturbation. The norm of the integral of the first-order remainder is at most epsilon times the Lp norm of the perturbation when that norm is sufficiently small.
